entry.title: AQuA: A Recursively Self-Improving Framework for Quantitative Trading Research

media:group.media:title: AQuA: A Recursively Self-Improving Framework for Quantitative Trading Research
media:group.media:description:
AQuA, from Princeton University, Ant Group and Stanford, is two independent AI research agents for quantitative trading — one discovers alpha factors on crypto, the other develops time-series models on US equities — and neither can leak future information into its own experiments. Each agent works inside a sealed sandbox: the data splits, feature and label definitions, and evaluator are fixed before iteration begins, and the agent can only emit a constrained factor expression or a single config diff. The paper documents the failure this design answers: an earlier permissive loop let an agent write a volume ratio that a reviewer agent approved, but whose denominator read through the end of the day. Results: a combined factor IC of about 0.190 on a crypto five-minute universe, a per-stock IC of +0.0843 on US equities versus +0.0613 for a GRU, and a dollar-neutral long/short book with a held-out Sharpe of +2.15 sector-neutral, +2.50 with causal volatility targeting, and +2.00 under a fully causal walk-forward — positive in every year from 2021 to 2025 at a 2 bps two-leg cost.
Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/09/01/aqua-a-two-part-agentic-framework-for-autonomous-factor-discovery/
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12841

entry.title: This 3B Model Reads Your Screen — And Runs On Your Phone

media:group.media:title: This 3B Model Reads Your Screen — And Runs On Your Phone
media:group.media:description:
Liquid AI just released LFM2.5-VL-3B, a 3.1-billion-parameter vision-language model that reads digital screens, grounds objects to coordinates, and calls tools — all while fitting in roughly 3GB of memory. It scores 80.7 on ScreenSpot-v2, lifts RefCOCO grounding from 57.1 to 87.9 over the previous release, and averages 69.4 across 28 vision benchmarks, matching models with 50% more parameters. It decodes 228 tokens/second on an Apple M5 Max and 20 tokens/second on a Galaxy S26 Ultra, with about 34ms to first token on an H100. Weights are open in native, GGUF, ONNX, and MLX formats, with day-one support in llama.cpp, vLLM, MLX, and SGLang. One catch worth knowing before you build on it: the LFM Open License is Apache-based, but free commercial use ends at $10M in annual revenue.
Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/08/13/liquid-ai-lfm2-5-vl-3b-on-device-vision-language-model/

entry.title: NVIDIA Just Released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard — Making AI Agents 4x Faster

media:group.media:title: NVIDIA Just Released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard — Making AI Agents 4x Faster
media:group.media:description:
NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open 30B mixture-of-experts model with just 3B active parameters, built for the execution layer of always-on AI agents — the tool calls, validation, and subagent delegation that eat most of an agent's token budget. This video breaks down how the hybrid Mamba-2 + MoE + Attention architecture, speculative decoding with the DSpark and DFlash drafters, and an NVFP4 checkpoint combine to deliver up to 4x faster output and 30% faster completion of 10,000 PinchBench tasks versus Qwen3.6 35B, all on a single H100 or DGX Spark with a 1M-token context window. It also covers NeMo Switchyard, NVIDIA's open source routing library, whose escalation router cut costs 74% in LangChain's 145-task benchmark by sending only 7% of calls to a frontier model.
Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/08/11/nvidia-ai-releases-nemotron-3-5-lightning-and-nemo-switchyard/

entry.title: Meta Just Released Muse Glimmer: A 30B Open-Weights Agentic Model That Runs on Local Device

media:group.media:title: Meta Just Released Muse Glimmer: A 30B Open-Weights Agentic Model That Runs on Local Device
media:group.media:description:
Meta AI released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter agentic model under Apache 2.0 that's built to run on hardware you already own. At full precision it would need over 55GB of memory; four-bit quantization drops the language model under 20GB, so it fits a single 24GB consumer GPU or an M-series Max Mac at 1.0% accuracy degradation. A block-diffusion drafter called DFlash proposes 16 tokens per forward pass and the main model verifies them in parallel, taking decode speed from 74.9 to 233.4 tokens per second on an RTX 5090 — 3.1x faster. It beats Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on MCP Atlas, DeepSearch QA and SWE-Bench Pro, but trails Qwen on OSWorld-Verified and TerminalBench, so it's a better fit for agent scaffolds than autonomous GUI control. This video walks through the architecture, the training pipeline, both engineering fixes, every benchmark table, the safety ratings, and whether you can actually deploy it today.....
Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/08/10/meta-ai-releases-muse-glimmer/
Model weights: https://huggingface.co/collections/meta-models/muse-glimmer

entry.title: LingBot-VA 2.0: The Robot Brain That Predicts and Acts in Real Time

media:group.media:title: LingBot-VA 2.0: The Robot Brain That Predicts and Acts in Real Time
media:group.media:description:
Ant Group's Robbyant has released LingBot-VA 2.0, a video-action foundation model built from scratch for robot control rather than fine-tuned from a video generator. It places world states and actions in one semantic latent space, drives a causal diffusion transformer with a sparse mixture-of-experts video stream (128 experts, top-8), and uses "Foresight Reasoning" to predict the next action chunk while executing the current one — re-grounding on every real observation. A four-stage inference stack cuts per-chunk latency from 927 ms to 142 ms, lifting asynchronous control from 35 Hz to 225 Hz. On RoboTwin 2.0 it edges past strong baselines, though the gain over version 1.0 is a modest 1.4 points.

entry.title: MuScriptor: The Open Model That Turns Any Song Into MIDI (Kyutai + Mirelo)

media:group.media:title: MuScriptor: The Open Model That Turns Any Song Into MIDI (Kyutai + Mirelo)
media:group.media:description:
Kyutai and Mirelo just released MuScriptor, an open-weight model that transcribes full multi-instrument music — from classical to heavy metal — straight into MIDI. In this video we break down how it works: a decoder-only Transformer trained in three stages (synthetic pre-training, fine-tuning on 170k real recordings, and GRPO-like reinforcement learning), reading a mel-spectrogram and predicting note events for pitch, timing, and instrument. We cover the benchmark gains over YourMT3+ (Multi F1 of 48.2 vs 21.9), why training on real audio beats synthetic MIDI, optional instrument conditioning, and how to run it yourself in a few lines.

entry.title: This AI World Model Ran for 60 Minutes Without Falling Apart

media:group.media:title: This AI World Model Ran for 60 Minutes Without Falling Apart
media:group.media:description:
Robbyant, Ant Group's embodied-intelligence unit, has open-sourced LingBot-World-Infinity — a 14B causal video world model you steer in real time with WASD, camera moves, and text events. Most interactive world models smear after a few minutes, because each generated frame feeds back into the next and errors compound. Robbyant attacks that at the attention mask. The Mixture of Bidirectional and Autoregressive (MoBA) mask appends a bidirectional full-attention block to the teacher forcing mask, stopping the model from leaning on context instead of predicting frames. Distribution matching distillation then runs over long self-rollout trajectories, so the student trains on the state distribution its own predictions induce. On top sits a Director-Pilot harness: a VLM proposes event cards, and the Diffusion Transformer renders them. The result is a single 60-minute uninterrupted session spanning 20 distinct scenarios.....
Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/07/09/meet-lingbot-world-infinity-an-open-causal-world-model-with-an-agentic-harness/

entry.title: NVIDIA Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B: 2x Throughput From Compressing a Hybrid MoE

media:group.media:title: NVIDIA Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B: 2x Throughput From Compressing a Hybrid MoE
media:group.media:description:
NVIDIA released Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B, a compressed variant of Nemotron-3-Super. The parent model drops from 120.7B total and 12.8B active parameters to 75.3B and 9.3B, while keeping its 88-block hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE layout intact. On a single 8xB200 node, it delivers 2.03x the server throughput of Super at a floor of 100 tokens per second per user. On one H100 at 1M-token context, sustainable concurrency rises from 1 request to 8. In this video we walk through Iterative Puzzle, the architecture search method behind it, the throughput tables, and the accuracy the compression actually costs. Arena-Hard-V2 drops 4.2 points and SWE-Bench drops 2.6, while RULER and AA-LCR stay within roughly 1 to 2 points.
Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/07/09/nvidia-releases-nemotron-labs-3-puzzle-75b-a9b-a-compressed-hybrid-moe-llm-delivering-2-03x-server-throughput-at-matched-user-throughput/

entry.title: Why LingBot-VLA 2.0 Brings DeepSeek-Style MoE Routing to Robotics

media:group.media:title: Why LingBot-VLA 2.0 Brings DeepSeek-Style MoE Routing to Robotics
media:group.media:description:
Ant Group's Robbyant has open-sourced LingBot-VLA 2.0, a 6B vision-language-action model built to close the gap between lab benchmarks and real robot deployment. It is pretrained on roughly 60,000 hours of data — 50,000 hours of robot trajectories spanning 20 robot configurations, plus 10,000 hours of egocentric human video — and maps every embodiment into a single 55-dimensional canonical action space covering arms, end-effectors, grippers, dexterous hands, waists, heads, and mobile bases. Two design choices carry most of the gain: a sparse Mixture-of-Experts action expert with DeepSeek-V3-style auxiliary-loss-free routing, and dual-query distillation, where a current query and a future query are supervised by LingBot-Depth for geometry and DINO-Video for causal temporal dynamics. On the GM-100 bimanual benchmark in a generalist setting, it reaches 66.2 / 34.4 progress score and success rate on AgileX Cobot Magic and 34.6 / 15.6 on Galaxea R1Pro, ahead of π0.5 and LingBot-VLA 1.0, and it leads π0.5 on both long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks in-domain and out-of-distribution. In this video we break down the data pipeline, the unified action space, the MoE architecture, the benchmark results, and how to run the 6B checkpoint — which ships on Hugging Face and ModelScope under Apache-2.0.
Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/07/08/lingbot-vla-2-0/

entry.title: LingBot-Vision: Ant Group's 1B Boundary-Centric Vision Model That Beats 7B DINOv3 on Depth

media:group.media:title: LingBot-Vision: Ant Group's 1B Boundary-Centric Vision Model That Beats 7B DINOv3 on Depth
media:group.media:description:
Ant Group's Robbyant open-sourced LingBot-Vision, a 1B self-supervised Vision Transformer that treats image boundaries as a native pretraining signal instead of a downstream output. It's trained with "masked boundary modeling" — the teacher forces boundary tokens into the mask and supervises them with a categorical boundary field, so geometry and semantics co-emerge.
It posts the best NYU-Depth v2 RMSE (0.296) of every model compared, ahead of the 7B DINOv3, on a corpus 10× smaller. The 0.3B distilled student matches 7B DINOv3 on depth with ~23× fewer parameters, and swapping the encoder into LingBot-Depth 2.0 leads 14 depth-completion benchmarks. Weights are Apache-2.0 in ViT-g/L/B/S sizes.
In this video: what it is → how masked boundary modeling works → benchmarks → how to load it → LingBot-Depth 2.0 → takeaways.
Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/07/07/ant-groups-robbyant-open-sources-lingbot-vision-a-1b-boundary-centric-vision-foundation-model-for-dense-spatial-perception/

entry.title: DeepSeek-V4 Explained: Hybrid CSA and HCA Attention That Cuts KV Cache to 10% at One Million Tokens

media:group.media:title: DeepSeek-V4 Explained: Hybrid CSA and HCA Attention That Cuts KV Cache to 10% at One Million Tokens
media:group.media:description:
DeepSeek-AI has released DeepSeek-V4, a preview series of two open-source Mixture-of-Experts language models — DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T parameters, 49B activated) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B parameters, 13B activated) — both natively supporting one-million-token contexts by combining Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA) in a hybrid interleaved architecture that reduces single-token inference FLOPs to 27% and KV cache to 10% of DeepSeek-V3.2 at 1M tokens, alongside Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) for stable residual learning, the Muon optimizer for faster convergence, and FP4 quantization-aware training on MoE expert weights and the CSA indexer QK path; post-training replaces mixed RL with On-Policy Distillation from 10+ domain-specific experts trained via SFT and GRPO, yielding a unified model that achieves a Codeforces rating of 3206 and 57.9 Pass@1 on SimpleQA Verified, with all weights publicly available on Hugging Face.
Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/04/24/deepseek-ai-releases-deepseek-v4-compressed-sparse-attention-and-heavily-compressed-attention-enable-one-million-token-contexts/

entry.title: Moonshot AI Open-Sources Kimi K2.6 with Native Multimodal MoE Architecture and Agent Swarm Scaling

media:group.media:title: Moonshot AI Open-Sources Kimi K2.6 with Native Multimodal MoE Architecture and Agent Swarm Scaling
media:group.media:description:
Moonshot AI has open-sourced Kimi K2.6, a native multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 1 trillion total parameters, 32 billion activated per token, a 256K context window, and a MoonViT vision encoder — released under a Modified MIT License. Built for production agentic workloads, K2.6 delivers strong long-horizon coding (185% throughput gain on a 13-hour autonomous engineering task), an Agent Swarm scaling to 300 sub-agents across 4,000 coordinated steps, a Skills feature that converts documents into reusable format templates, and Claw Groups — a research preview enabling humans and heterogeneous agents from any device to collaborate in a shared swarm. On benchmarks, K2.6 scores 54.0 on HLE-Full with tools, 58.6 on SWE-Bench Pro, and 89.6 on LiveCodeBench (v6), deployable via vLLM, SGLang, or KTransformers....
